mitigation_mechanism: Linear tree plantings act on drought through different routes, and the evidence reports both a gain and a loss. Live fences of species such as Gliricidia sepium and Leucaena leucocephala supply high-quality livestock fodder in the dry season, when pasture is scarce [ev_drought_hazard_moran18_1]. For crops beside shelterbelts, earlier work cited in a temperate alley-cropping study found greater yield losses near shelterbelts in dry years because of competition [ev_crop_yield_majaura25_3]. Between these, the FAO Senegal review reports no clear consensus on windbreak hedges in drought: some studies find higher crop yields near windbreaks in drier years, while others judge the hedges could harm non-irrigated crops [ev_drought_hazard_faosen24_17].
caveats: The sides largely answer different questions. The gain is fodder for livestock from live fences [ev_drought_hazard_moran18_1]; the loss is crop yield next to shelterbelts, where trees compete with the crop for water in dry years [ev_crop_yield_majaura25_3]. Which one matters depends on whether the farm's drought exposure is in its herd or its field crops, and on the linear practice chosen. For crops alone the windbreak literature is itself split, as the Senegal review states [ev_drought_hazard_faosen24_17]. All the units are reviews or citations of earlier studies with no effect sizes, so neither side is better evidenced than the other. The windbreak unit is from Senegal (lower-middle income), the live-fence unit is a pantropical review with no income group recorded, and the shelterbelt finding is temperate evidence [ev_drought_hazard_faosen24_17, ev_drought_hazard_moran18_1, ev_crop_yield_majaura25_3].

mitigation_mechanism: Linear tree plantings act on drought through different routes, and the evidence reports both a gain and a loss. Live fences of species such as Gliricidia sepium and Leucaena leucocephala supply high-quality livestock fodder in the dry season, when pasture is scarce [ev_drought_hazard_moran18_1]. For crops beside shelterbelts, earlier work cited in a temperate alley-cropping study found greater yield losses near shelterbelts in dry years because of competition [ev_crop_yield_majaura25_3]. Between these, the FAO Senegal review reports no clear consensus on windbreak hedges in drought: some studies find higher crop yields near windbreaks in drier years, while others judge the hedges could harm non-irrigated crops [ev_drought_hazard_faosen24_17].
caveats: The sides largely answer different questions. The gain is fodder for livestock from live fences [ev_drought_hazard_moran18_1]; the loss is crop yield next to shelterbelts, where trees compete with the crop for water in dry years [ev_crop_yield_majaura25_3]. Which one matters depends on whether the farm's drought exposure is in its herd or its field crops, and on the linear practice chosen. For crops alone the windbreak literature is itself split, as the Senegal review states [ev_drought_hazard_faosen24_17]. All the units are reviews or citations of earlier studies with no effect sizes, so neither side is better evidenced than the other. The windbreak unit is from Senegal (lower-middle income), the live-fence unit is a pantropical review with no income group recorded, and the shelterbelt finding is temperate evidence [ev_drought_hazard_faosen24_17, ev_drought_hazard_moran18_1, ev_crop_yield_majaura25_3]. Only some units come from rainfed cropping systems [ev_drought_hazard_faosen24_17]; the others record no or a different farming system and are applied by default [ev_drought_hazard_moran18_1, ev_crop_yield_majaura25_3].

mitigation_mechanism: On paired on-farm plots in Ethiopia's Central Rift Valley, wheat under Faidherbia albida crowns gave up to 85% more grain than open-field wheat in 2015, an El Niño year in which both yields were low [ev_crop_yield_sida18_2]. Parkland hydraulic redistribution lets crops use deep soil moisture reached only by tree roots [ev_soil_water_retention_vannoordwijk21_3], and the Kenyan compiler for Farmer Managed Natural Regeneration (FMNR) judges that it improves micro-climate and soil moisture and so mitigates drought impacts [ev_drought_hazard_wocat_507_2019_drought_impacts]. In Lempira, Honduras, crops on farms using the Quesungual agroforestry system withstood the El Niño-associated drought of 1997, while farmers who had not adopted it suffered crop losses [ev_crop_yield_chaudhury11_3].
caveats: The Ethiopian paired-plot study is the measured result here: a drought-year comparison reported as an 'up to' figure, with the normal-season gain reported separately in the same study [ev_crop_yield_sida18_2]. The other literature unit is a review describing a soil-water process in West African Sahel parklands, used as a component of drought impact rather than a measured drought loss [ev_soil_water_retention_vannoordwijk21_3]. The FMNR unit is a single compiler rating of a slight benefit, not a measurement [ev_drought_hazard_wocat_507_2019_drought_impacts]. The Honduran point is an earlier observation cited in an ICRAF working paper [ev_crop_yield_chaudhury11_3].
